newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr remains top-heavy vs yen despite MOF comments.
newsitem.headline: Dlr remains top-heavy vs yen despite MOF comments.

text.p: 0512 GMT --- *Dollar remained top-heavy after earlier edging up on short-covering following reported comments around noon by MOF officials that an excessively weak or excessively strong yen is undesirable.
*Dealers said MOF comments were not strong enough to push up dollar above 112 yen and traders started selling in afternoon, with sentiment still bearish for dollar.
*Earlier, Eisuke Sakakibara, head of Ministry of Finance's International Finance Bureau, was quoted as saying by Jiji news agency that an excessively weak or strong yen is undesirable.

*Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka also later said that excessively weak or strong yen was undesirable and that MOF would deal with foreign exchange movements in an appropriate manner, Jiji reported.
*"Short-covering pushed the dollar up following Sakakibara's comments... But the dollar did not go back above 112 yen and traders started selling," a trust bank dealer said.

*Dealers said a dip below 110 yen is in sight while no substantial bids expected on downside amid bearish dollar sentiment and lingering concerns over Japan's trade surplus ahead of Denver summit on June 20-22.
*Dollar was sharply lower against yen at midday in Tokyo after a wave of selling by overseas and Japanese players.
*Dollar selling gained momentum following remarks by U.S. Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers that Japan should foster demand-led recovery and avoid running up external surpluses.
*Dollar briefly fell below 111 yen to its lowest level since November 20, 1996, as U.S. funds and Japanese interbank players rushed to sell dollars following Summers' remarks.
